facts.fact_text: The applicants attempted to participate in a public event in support of LGBTI people.
The public event in support of LGBTI people was authorised to take place on 12 October 2013 in St Petersburg.
The applicants were among the group of participants arrested by the police at the public event on 12 October 2013.
The public event on 12 October 2013 in St Petersburg was disrupted by violent counter-demonstrators.
The police present at the public event on 12 October 2013 arrested a group of participants in the event.
The applicants were among the group of participants arrested by the police at the public event on 12 October 2013.
The applicants were transferred to a police station following their arrest at the public event on 12 October 2013.
The applicants were charged with disorderly misconduct (use of foul language), an offence under Article 20.1 of the Federal Code of Administrative Offences.

The Primorskiy District Court of St Petersburg considered that the first applicant's arrest and transfer to the police station had been lawful because she had refused to show her ID documents to the police.
The St Petersburg City Court stressed that there had been tension between the participants of the gathering and counter-demonstrators during the event on 12 October 2013.
The St Petersburg City Court stressed that there had been a breach of public order during the event on 12 October 2013.
The St Petersburg City Court stressed that there had been tension between the participants of the gathering and counter-demonstrators during the event on 12 October 2013.
The St Petersburg City Court stressed that there had been a breach of public order during the event on 12 October 2013.
The St Petersburg City Court held that the first applicant's arrest and transfer to the police station had been justified for the purposes of facilitating subsequent administrative proceedings.

The St Petersburg City Court held that the fact that the administrative proceedings against the first applicant had later been terminated had not invalidated the lawfulness of the first applicant's arrest.
The second applicant claimed that the police had failed to ensure public order during the gathering on 12 October 2013.
The second applicant claimed that the police had failed to ensure the safety of participants in the gathering on 12 October 2013.

The applicants complained under Article 11 of the Convention in conjunction with Article 14 of the Convention that the police arrested only the participants in the LGBTI public event and disregarded the breaches of public order by their opponents.
